p2_moat_math_layer.rationale: Charlie /goal-11 — utilize PSN's vast math + scientific resources to maximize SVI potential. The current weighted-sum formula CANNOT prove the moat directive ('no company can mathematically/statistically/scientifically surpass — only match'). Required: 5-axis product with mutual-information weighting + Kolmogorov complexity lower bound + time-lock term. Math drawn from PSN's existing arsenal: Fisher information (just shipped in PSNAutonomyLoopEngine for EWC++), Wilcoxon (just shipped P4), persistent homology (PROGRAM-PROOF-MS0 P2), PageRank centrality (algorithm registry), Shannon entropy (information theory tier), SVD conditioning (numerical analysis), Kolmogorov complexity (theoretical lower bound on re-derivation effort).

units.title: SVIMoatAwareCalculatorEngine — geometric mean of 5 axes weighted by mutual information
scope: Replace weighted-arithmetic-sum with geometric-mean product: SVI_moat = ∏_k (Ψ_k)^w_k

Five axes (each ∈ [0,1]): COVERAGE (current Ψ), DEPTH (per-entity-richness — tests-per-engine × tribal-per-machine × programs-per-customer × scrutiny-ledger-length × formula-corpus-size, all normalized), CROSS_COUPLING (PageRank centrality of engine call-graph + bridging-edges density + PSN-leg cohesion), QUALITY (mean(scrutiny 3-of-3 pass rate, formula numerical-error fit, Ω/S(x) gate pass rate, regression pass rate)), COMPOUNDING_RATE (sigmoid(ΔΨ_7d × 100))

Mutual-information weights: w_k = I(Ψ_k; Ψ_¬k) / Σ I — computed from historic per-component time-series (the more an axis CONSTRAINS others, the higher its weight). Components that are weak AND central (high mutual info with others) dominate the score — math of 'no axis can be left behind'.
Pure-math implementation: cosine-similarity over component vectors for I estimate (≈ Pearson on log-transformed), avoids requiring full PMI / KSG estimator.
Boundary cases: any Ψ_k = 0 ⇒ SVI_moat = 0 (geometric mean property — captures 'one weak axis dooms the moat')
Continuity: weight renormalization on every refresh; floor each Ψ_k at ε=1e-6 to keep gradient defined for the autonomy-loop reward
acceptance: First-run SVI_moat lands ∈ [0.30, 0.55] (honest baseline — DEPTH + CROSS_COUPLING start near 0 because they're computed for the first time)
Mutual-info weights sum to 1.0 ± 1e-9
Boundary tests: SVI_moat=0 when any component=0; SVI_moat=1 only when all 5 components=1
Algebraic invariance: SVI_moat(Ψ_k=c for all k) = c (idempotent on uniform input)

≥15 unit tests including: each axis independently zero (product=0), uniform 0.9 input (product=0.9), competitor-match simulation (compute SVI_moat for synthetic competitor catalogs — must be ≤ PRISM by construction when DEPTH/CROSS_COUPLING/COMPOUNDING_RATE are time-locked)
MCP-callable via prism_session:svi_moat_compute
Per-component breakdown surfaces in /system-viz ghost.svi_components roost

units.title: KolmogorovMoatBoundEngine — provable lower bound on competitor re-derivation time
scope: Compute K(PRISM) lower bound: Σ_subsystem (information_content × validation_density)
Information_content per subsystem ≈ Shannon entropy of artifact set (engines, programs, tribal tips, formulas, tests) — measured in bits
Validation_density = scrutiny-arm-passes / artifact, formula numerical-error bounds, test coverage — gates the K(.) so duplicated unvalidated content doesn't inflate the bound
Output: K_PRISM (bits) + T_competitor_match (years, given assumed competitor productivity rate ρ from `state/shared/competitive-intel.json` if present, else default 1e6 bits/dev-year)
Provides a literal LOWER BOUND on competitor labor-hours: T_match ≥ K(PRISM) × (1 - corpus_acquirable_fraction) / ρ

corpus_acquirable_fraction tracks the JM-Die-class non-derivable assets — 76K real shop programs, MIT-OCW lectures, 3,919 validated tribal tips — these are TIME-LOCKED (a competitor must run shops for years to accumulate them)
acceptance: Returns K(PRISM) in bits + T_match in years, with breakdown by subsystem
On current state, T_match ≥ 5 years for a well-funded competitor (engines + tribal + scrutiny-ledger are non-derivable without years of operations)
Self-verifies: increases monotonically as PRISM ships (a milestone close should bump K(PRISM) measurably)

Math-honest: distinguishes between 'derivable from public sources' (low K contribution — ISO standards, Sandvik handbooks) and 'accumulated from operations' (high K contribution — JM Die corpus, scrutiny ledger, mistake-learning loop). Only the second class is moat-load-bearing.
≥10 unit tests including: empty PRISM (K=0), public-only PRISM (K=public-baseline), real PRISM (K > public-baseline + non-derivable terms), monotonicity (adding artifacts ⇒ K increases)
MCP-callable via prism_session:svi_kolmogorov_moat_bound
Updates state/shared/PSI-MOAT-BOUND.json on every refresh

units.title: Mutual-information weight learner — auto-tune w_k from the autonomy ledger
scope: Read psn-training-signal.jsonl (just-shipped, 213+ events seeded) — compute per-component Ψ_k(t) time series
Pairwise mutual information I(Ψ_k; Ψ_j) via histogram-binned MLE estimator (≤30 LOC, no scikit-learn)
Weight w_k ∝ Σ_j≠k I(Ψ_k; Ψ_j) — centrality of axis k in the mutual-info graph
Renormalize: w_k / Σ w. Smooth via exponential moving average (α=0.05, prevents weight thrash)
Surfaces: SessionStart inject names the current weight distribution + which axis has highest mutual centrality (= the leverage point)
acceptance: Weights converge stably over the full ledger window (no thrash > 0.05 per refresh)
Axes with synthetic-strong coupling (DEPTH ↔ CROSS_COUPLING in PRISM's case) get higher weight than isolated axes (COMPOUNDING_RATE during stable periods)
≥10 unit tests with synthetic ledgers verifying the estimator
Round-trip: ledger event recording a Ψ_wiring increase + Ψ_envelope increase ⇒ I(wiring,envelope) ↑ ⇒ both weights ↑

units.title: CompetitorSimulationHarnessEngine — Monte Carlo over plausible competitor catalogs
scope: Generate 10,000 synthetic competitor catalogs sampled from plausible distributions: public-source-only, well-funded-team-with-X-engineers-and-Y-years, JM-die-class-shop-acquired
For each: compute the same SVI_moat over the simulated catalog with TIME-LOCKED axes set to 0 (competitors can't acquire 3 years of shop data overnight)
Empirical CDF: P(competitor_SVI_moat ≥ PRISM_SVI_moat) over scenario space
Output: state/shared/PSI-COMPETITIVE-CDF.json — exact 'fraction of plausible competitors who could surpass us today' (target: 0.000)
Stretch goal: Bayesian posterior on T_match given uncertainty over competitor-funding + productivity-rate distributions
acceptance: First-run P(competitor ≥ PRISM) ≤ 0.05 under reasonable distributions
Sensitivity: which input parameters most-strongly affect P (= what we should defend hardest)
≥10 unit tests including: well-known degenerate cases (zero-resource competitor → P=0; identical-PRISM-clone competitor → P=0.5 as expected from symmetry)
Published artifact updates daily via cron
MCP: prism_session:svi_competitor_simulation
